legal name come from? How and why did it arrive on those letters? Did either of the two

before formal service? Why did they not wait the five days until April 27, when one court
temporarily stayed discovery, or the nine days until May 1, when discovery in the other
action was temporarily stayed? Where did the urgency come from?

against all Defendants, for letters sent to frighten me out of my own lawsuits; defamation,
intentional infliction of emotional distress, and insulting words against Hall and NCMEC,
for what the letters said and to whom. This Complaint adds NCMEC's Chief Legal Officer,
Panayiota Souras, who, on information and belief, approved the wording of the letters and
authorized Hall to send them before formal service. The defamation and insulting-words
counts are also asserted against Souras; Count IIl remains against Hall and NCMEC.
This case is about two letters and the lawyer who wrote them. On April 22, 2026, Katie Hall
Corporate Counsel of the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children, the organization this
country trusts to track crimes against children tied my name to "two CyberTipline reports." She

chose the words. She signed both letters. She sent them. Each one opened by telling me it was
answering a subpoena. No subpoena had been served. Not one. There was no process, court order,
or obligation behind the words Hall put on that letterhead.
The CyberTipline exists to catch people who hurt children. Federal law requires companies to
report to it. Law enforcement can be given what it holds. Everyone understands what it means
when that name appears above a man's name. That is why those letters landed on me the way they
did.
I was not a defendant. I was the plaintiff one man, without a lawyer, suing Meta Platforms, Inc.
and others in the Middle District of Florida. Case No. 6:26 cv 00376-AGM DCI. Case No. 6:26-
ev 00286 AGM DCI. I had asked one question in both: did anyone connected to the July 4, 2022
shutdown of my account send a CyberTipline report about me? I had noticed depositions for April
28, 29, and 30 to ask it under oath. One notice told Accenture, in writing, that its witness would
have to answer that question.
On April 21, 2026, every defendant in both cases moved to shut down discovery and stop the
depositions. The letters came the next day. Each one carried the caption and case number of one
of my lawsuits. Each one answered the exact question my depositions were set to ask outside
discovery, unsworn, with no one to cross examine. And each one left out everything a man would
need to test it: who reported, when, what number, which identifier, which platform, what came of
it. The letters came to me alone. No court was copied. No lawyer was copied.
Consider what was true on April 22. No subpoena had been served. No court had ordered Hall to
do anything. I had not asked for an early answer of waived service. The motions filed the day
before were undecided. The ruling dates the movants demanded had not come. The depositions
they were trying to stop had not happened. Nothing required Hall to send those letters that day.
Nothing required Hall to send them at all.
And Hall knew who she was writing to. Before those letters went out, she had either read the
pleadings in the 286 Action or been handed what was in them. Those pleadings said that I am a
survivor of childhood sexual abuse. They said that putting my name next to the language of child
exploitation had already hurt me. Hall is the lawyer for the clearinghouse this country built to track
crimes against children. She knows what that name does to a man.
She sent the letters anyway. Who told her to send them, and what was said before they went out,
are answers kept in NCMEC's files and Meta's, not mine.
I read the letters on April 28, 2026 the day my first deposition was supposed to go forward, and
did not. I understood what I was reading: that federal records now tied my name to the sexual
exploitation of children, and that law enforcement could come for me. I was afraid of being

decided on that motion.
